text: Phosphate deficiency induces expression of CCD7/D17 and CCD8/D10 via PHR2 in cereals, elevating strigolactone production and apoplastic exudation into the rhizosphere.
Exuded strigolactones act as chemical branching factors for arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi at picomolar to nanomolar thresholds.
Strigolactones bind D14 to recruit D3 and trigger proteasome-mediated degradation of the transcriptional repressor D53.

Strigolactones promote root hair elongation through both ethylene-dependent and an autonomous ethylene-independent transcriptional branch, demonstrating complex multi-pathway regulation rather than simple linear dependency.
